item.description:
Scribe finds pieces saved twice and keeps one copy, and a PDF's find bar and notes stay out of each other's way.

  • New: Settings ▸ Library ▸ Saved twice lists pieces in your library more than once. Keep one copy of each; the others go to the bin, and the one you keep takes their place on the stack, their tags and their category.
  • Fixed: saving a PDF that was already in the library kept a second copy, even with Duplicates set to Skip.
  • Fixed: a book or link saved twice at once, such as two copies in one folder, could get past the duplicate check.
  • Duplicates are recognised more widely: a book with the same ISBN, or the same title with its author written differently, and a link with tracking parameters or "www." added. Two editions of a book with different ISBNs stay apart.
  • Fixed: with a PDF's notes open, the find bar sat off-centre and partly over the notes.
  • Fixed: selecting text near the top of the page while finding could put the highlight picker on top of the find bar.
  • The notes beside a PDF mark the highlight you jumped to, and keep it in view, until you pick another.

Closing Find in a PDF no longer opens the highlight colours.

  • Fixed: clicking Find's close button or arrows in a PDF opened the highlight colours, as if you'd selected the match yourself.

Drops all go through the Save sheet, failed imports clean up after themselves, finding text in long PDFs stays smooth, and the updater picks up Sparkle's security fixes.

  • Removed an old, unused way of searching the library; searching works as before.
  • What’s New shows the latest couple of releases instead of Scribe’s whole history; “All release notes” in the same card shows every release.
  • After skipping several updates, What’s New shows the newest two rather than every version since.
  • Clicking a link in an essay or book now only opens web and email links. Links to files on your Mac or to other apps' custom schemes are ignored instead of being handed to macOS.
  • Fixed: adding a file that isn't a readable PDF left a hidden copy of it in Scribe's library folder. A failed PDF or web page import now removes everything it saved.
  • Scribe's built-in updater now uses Sparkle 2.9.6, which fixes two security issues in how updates are installed.
  • Dropping files or links onto Today, a department or the Catalogue now opens the Save sheet with its progress, retry and category choices, the same as dropping anywhere else in the window. Before, those pages saved drops silently in the background, with no word if one failed.
  • Find in a PDF now searches once you pause typing, in the background, and shows matches as they're found. Typing a short word in a long PDF no longer freezes the reader.
  • Very common words stop at 1,000 matches, shown as "1 of 1000+".
